speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the current successful job matching rate of MyCareersFuture.sg; (b) whether there are plans to introduce vernacular versions of the platform to help our older jobseekers; and (c) what are the plans to increase the job listings by smaller companies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether an update can be provided on the job match success rate of the Jobs Bank for Singaporeans; and (b) what measures are being implemented to enable the measurement of job match success rates of the Jobs Bank and MyCareersFuture.sg for the purpose of assessing the returns on investment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Workforce Singapore (WSG) helps match jobseekers with employers through the Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister, are you taking Question Nos 12 and 13 together?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Yes, Sir, thank you for pointing it out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MyCareersFuture is one channel among several under Adapt and Grow.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is an online jobs marketplace that recently replaced the national Jobs Bank to help jobseekers and employers perform smarter and faster job searches.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Jobs Bank had been well utilised, notwithstanding the many other options available to employers and jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, the employers used the platform for job postings even if they were not required to under the Fair Consideration Framework.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are, therefore, looking at ways to better assess the effectiveness of MyCareersFuture in job matching, such as inferring placement rates, using administrative data.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We expect the proportion to be similar in MyCareersFuture.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The MyCareersFuture platform is more useful to jobseekers by having the widest possible range of job postings.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Employers, too, will prefer to post job openings on a platform that is accessed by more jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Therefore, instead of creating vernacular versions to cater to specific language users, our aim is to ensure ease-of-use of the platform for all users.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to serve users who are more comfortable communicating in vernacular languages through Workforce Singapore's Careers Connect and the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Employment and Employability Institute as they have career centres dotted across the island.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This includes providing guidance on online job searches so that these jobseekers, too, can eventually benefit from accessing opportunities through such avenues.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is the emphasis on success rate detracting the jobseeker from the fact that some of them may need to upgrade their skills, learn new skills, or are we paying too much attention on the ability of immediate matching, for example, they think "just because I list myself in the Jobs Bank, or I go to the Jobs Bank, I can therefore get a job"?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Sometimes, people may forget that you actually may need to go for different skills upgrading.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Then that journey may take a longer time.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, are we paying too much attention on success rate and not putting enough focus on getting yourselves trained and upgraded to acquire a new skillset?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I can assure the Member that we do not just focus on getting job matches.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think the starting point is that, if we want to get the jobseekers matched with the employers, we have to, first, start with the consideration of the jobseekers' needs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if they are job-ready, skills-ready, what they want is an efficient way to find out who is hiring, what the employers are looking for, and what salaries are on offer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Under those circumstances, MyCareersFuture.sg provides a channel which is free.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It does not charge for any of the features, unlike private portals, which charge for certain features.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It uses the latest in job-skills matching technology and points out, in fact, if the jobs come with Government schemes support, which no other portal will do.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The reason why we set up MyCareersFuture.sg is also because we know that, sometimes, some additional help is needed to match the employers' requirements by having a skills top-up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, therefore, our portal makes this clear to the jobseeker: you want the job, you like it, you may not have everything that the employer is looking for, but there is help available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The portal will point this out, and then with a click through, the jobseeker can find out what help is available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of course, the jobseekers are free to approach the employers through the portal or through other means.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, they follow up at networking events.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is why, quite often, they may secure the jobs without our knowledge.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But that is also the case with other portals.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we do not insist, right now, that either the employer or the jobseekers must close the loop and tell us that they have secured the job this way.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because if we insisted on that, we must ask if this inadvertently limits the number of jobs listed, or the number of jobseekers who use it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, whilst we are interested, we want to find out if there has been a job match, we do not yet insist on it primarily because we understand that there are sometimes follow-through, follow-up that can be taken through other avenues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: I just would like to ask for some further clarifications from the Minister about the fact that if you actually want something like MyCareersFuture to work, you need a systematic volume of participation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: So, if we do not have certain metrics about how successful the system is, so how do you get that volume of participation?

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: I am just asking this because I actually think it is a very good idea, but are there intermediate metrics other than the primary success rate?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In response to the Member's question, the Member is quite right.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There must be many users and there are two primary groups of users.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So that gives us a sense that it is quite an active marketplace.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our aim, of course, is to make it even more active and that we do so by improving the features making it even easier to use.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
